what_its_for: Salsalate is used to relieve pain, reduce swelling, and decrease stiffness caused by arthritis (such as rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis). It belongs to a group of medicines called salicylates, which work similarly to aspirin but may be gentler on the stomach.
how_to_take: Take salsalate by mouth with a full glass of water (8 ounces). You may take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush or chew them. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep a steady amount in your body. Do not take more than your doctor has prescribed.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 1,500 mg (1.5 grams) taken twice a day, OR 1,000 mg (1 gram) taken three times a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how well it works for you and whether you have any side effects. The maximum recommended daily dose is 3,000 mg (3 grams) per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT double up or take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store salsalate at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking salsalate, as it increases the risk of stomach bleeding. Do not take other pain relievers, aspirin, or anti-inflammatory drugs (like ibuprofen or naproxen) unless your doctor approves, as combining them can raise the risk of side effects. Avoid activities that require full alertness if you feel dizzy. Let all your doctors and dentists know you are taking salsalate before any procedure or new medication is prescribed.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: ringing or buzzing in your ears or hearing loss (this can be a sign the dose is too high), stomach pain, black or tarry stools, or vomiting blood (signs of stomach bleeding), skin rash, hives, or severe allergic reaction (difficulty breathing, swelling of face or throat), unusual bruising or bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), or signs of kidney problems (less urination, swelling in legs or feet).
when_it_works: You may begin to notice some relief from pain and stiffness within a few days of starting salsalate. However, the full benefits for arthritis — especially reduced swelling and improved joint movement — may take 2 to 4 weeks of regular use. It is important to keep taking it every day as directed, even if you feel better.
special_populations: Children and teenagers: Salsalate should NOT be given to children or teenagers with flu-like symptoms or chickenpox due to the risk of a rare but serious condition called Reye's syndrome. Pregnant women: Talk to your doctor before taking salsalate during pregnancy, especially during the last trimester, as it may harm the unborn baby. Breastfeeding: Salsalate passes into breast milk; talk to your doctor before using it while breastfeeding. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects such as stomach bleeding, dizziness, and kidney problems. Use with extra caution and close monitoring. Kidney or liver disease: Use with caution; your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely.
